/-!
# Erdős Problem 71

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/71](https://www.erdosproblems.com/71)
- [Bo77] Bollobás, Béla, *Cycles modulo $k$*. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1977), 97-98.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.
- [Er95] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and
  geometry*. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
- [Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*.
  Discrete Math. (1997), 227-231.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos71

/--
Is it true that for every infinite arithmetic progression $P$ which contains even numbers
there is some constant $c=c(P)$ such that every graph with average degree at least $c$
contains a cycle whose length is in $P$?

In [Er82e] Erdős credits this conjecture to himself and Burr. This has been proved by
Bollobás [Bo77]. The best dependence of the constant $c(P)$ is unknown.

The infinite arithmetic progression is encoded as a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ satisfying
`P.IsAPOfLength ⊤` (which forces a positive common difference), and "contains even numbers"
as the existence of an even element. The average degree of a finite simple graph is
`SimpleGraph.averageDegree`, i.e. $(\sum_v \deg v)/|V| \in \mathbb{Q}$, and a cycle whose
length is in $P$ is a cycle walk `w` with `w.length ∈ P`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jayyhk/erdos-lean/blob/110d489ed5c07e5b216453e092e9113127c98c9a/problems/71/Erdos71.lean"]
theorem erdos_71 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ P : Set ℕ, P.IsAPOfLength ⊤ → (∃ n ∈ P, Even n) →
      ∃ c : ℚ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
        [DecidableRel G.Adj], c ≤ G.averageDegree →
          ∃ (v : V) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length ∈ P := by
  sorry

end Erdos71

reformulations.difference: The Lean version quantifies over one-sided progressions P = {a + n·d : n ∈ ℕ} ⊆ ℕ with d ≥ 1 (a = 0 allowed), written `P.IsAPOfLength ⊤`. It asks for a cycle with `w.length ∈ P`, which also forces length ≥ a. The literature states the Burr–Erdős conjecture that Bollobás proved for residue classes instead. Sudakov–Verstraëte (EJC 24(1) #P1.7): for k, ℓ ∈ ℤ⁺ such that kℤ + ℓ contains even integers, every graph of average degree at least c_k(ℓ) contains a cycle of length ℓ mod k. A reader comparing the two might think the Lean version is stronger because of the implicit lower bound on the length.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (⇒) Given k ≥ 1 and ℓ with an even element in ℓ + kℕ, take P = {(ℓ mod k) + n·k}. P is an infinite AP, it contains an even number, and P ⊆ {L : L ≡ ℓ mod k}. (⇐) Given P = {a + n·d} (d ≥ 1) containing an even number, set k = d(2a+1), so k > a. If d is odd then k is odd; if d is even then a must be even. Either way a + kℕ contains an even number. Any L ≥ 0 with L ≡ a (mod k) has the form L = a + j·k with j ≥ 0, because a < k. So L = a + (j(2a+1))·d ∈ P. Both directions only use that the property S ↦ '∃ c, every finite graph with averageDegree ≥ c has a cycle of length in S' is monotone in S. I proved this in Lean in /workspace/review/equiv.lean: `Review71.oneSided_iff_residue` for any monotone Q, and `Review71.rhs_iff_residue` for the file's exact RHS against the residue-class form. Axioms used: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Also, 'kℤ+ℓ contains even integers' is equivalent to 'some ℓ + k·m with m ∈ ℕ is even' (both mean k odd or ℓ even).

review.notes:
The file has one declaration, `Erdos71.erdos_71`. Its right-hand side matches erdosproblems.com/71 word for word: every infinite AP P containing an even number has a constant c = c(P) such that every graph with average degree ≥ c has a cycle whose length is in P.

Checks in Lean (/workspace/review/scratch.lean and equiv.lean):
- `P.IsAPOfLength ⊤` on ℕ holds exactly when P = {a + n·d | n ∈ ℕ} with d > 0. The docstring's claim that it 'forces a positive common difference' is correct.
- An empty vertex type gets the junk value averageDegree = 0/0 = 0. This does no harm because c is existential, so any c > 0 excludes it.
- Complete graphs have unbounded average degree, so the hypothesis `c ≤ averageDegree` can always be met.
- `Walk.IsCycle` requires length ≥ 3. Mathlib's `averageDegree` equals 2|E|/|V| by the handshake lemma.
- The `[DecidableEq V]` binder is unused, since `averageDegree` does not take it. It is harmless.
- Restricting V to `Type` loses nothing for finite graphs.

Answer and status: `answer(True)` together with `research solved` matches the source ('solved in the affirmative and the proof verified in Lean'). The linked formal proof states exactly this right-hand side. The module references match the repository's other citations and the Crossref record for [Bo77].
